== Origin ==
According to shrine tradition, it was founded by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=En no Gyōja}} in {{ill|672|ab|672|af|672|als|672|am|672 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|672|ar|672|ary|672|ast|672|avk|672|az|672|azb|۶۷۲ (میلادی)|be|672|be_x_old|672|bg|672|bn|৬৭২|bpy|মারি ৬৭২|br|672|bs|672.|ca|672|cdo|672 nièng|ceb|672|ckb|٦٧٢|crh|672|cs|672|cv|672|cy|672|da|672|de|672|el|672|eml|672|eo|672|es|672|et|672|eu|672|fa|۶۷۲ (میلادی)|fi|672|fo|672|fr|672|frr|672|fy|672|ga|672|gan|672年|gd|672|gl|672|he|672|hi|672|hr|672.|ht|672 (almanak jilyen)|hu|672|hy|672|id|672|io|672|is|672|it|672|ja|672年|jv|672|ka|672|kk|672 жыл|ko|672년|la|672|lb|672|lij|672|lmo|672|lt|672 m.|lv|672. gads|map_bms|672|mdf|672|mg|672|mhr|672|mk|672|mr|इ.स. ६७२|mrj|672 и|ms|672|mzn|۶۷۲|nah|672|nap|672|nds|672|nds_nl|672|new|सन् ६७२|nl|672|nn|672|no|672|nrm|672|nso|672|oc|672|or|୬୭୨|os|672-æм аз|pl|672|pnb|672|pt|672|qu|672|ro|672|ru|672 год|rue|672|sa|६७२|scn|672|sd|672ع|se|672|sh|672.|shn|672|si|672|sk|672|sl|672|sq|672|sr|672|su|672|sv|672|sw|672|tg|Соли 672|th|พ.ศ. 1215|tk|672|tl|672|tly|672|tr|672|tt|672 ел|uk|672|ur|672ء|uz|672|vec|672|vi|672|war|672|wuu|672年|xmf|672|zh|672年|zh_min_nan|672 nî|zh_yue|672年|qid=Q30601}} ({{ill|Hakuhō|ja|白鳳|ru|Хакухо|zh|白鳳|qid=Q11580612}} 12). It appears in the '{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}' as "Shioyuhiko Shrine, Hiraka District, Dewa Province," i.e., a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}<ref name=akita/><ref name=jinjacho>[https://akita-jinjacho.sakura.ne.jp/tatsujin_etc/01_jinja/yokote/043_sioyuhiko.html "Shioyuhiko Shrine" official site of Akita Prefecture Shrine Office]</ref>. It seems originally to have been a hot-spring deity of Mount Ontake rising east of the Hiraka basin<ref name=akita/>, but under influence of {{ill|Kumano Three Shrines|ja|熊野三山|pl|Kumano Sanzan|ru|Три храма Кумано|zh|熊野三山|qid=Q10403700|lt=Kumano}}-line {{ill|Shugendō|ca|Shugendo|cs|Šugendó|de|Shugendō|es|Shugendō|fr|Shugendō|it|Shugendō|ja|修験道|ko|수험도|pl|Shugendō|pt|Shugendō|ru|Сюгэндо|simple|Shugendō|sk|Šugendó|sr|Šugendo|tr|Shugendō|zh|修驗道|qid=Q1483875}}<ref name=akita/> it came to be called "Kumano-dō" in the medieval period. Likely for that reason, Hayatama-no-Mikoto is enshrined.

After a period of decline<ref name=akita/>, the Otomo family, priests of {{ill|Horowasan Haushiwake Shrine|ja|保呂羽山波宇志別神社|qid=Q11385699}} (another Shikinaisha in the same district), served as {{ill|Bettō|es|Bettō|fa|بتتو|fr|Bettō|it|Bettō|ja|別当|pt|Bettō|qid=Q2900274}}, while the Minashi family in charge of kagura managed it in practice. == Outside/associated shrines ==
* '''Satomiya''': '''Shioyuhiko Tsurugaike Shrine''' (Tsurugaike, Tsuchibuchi, Sannai, Yokote)
* '''Inner sanctuary''': '''Shirataki Kannon''' (Kannonzawa, Oomatsukawa, Sannai, Yokote)

== Scenic / historic points ==
* The foothills of Mount Ontake where this shrine stands are the northern limit of large clusters of {{ill|Camellia rusticana|ja|ユキツバキ|vi|Camellia rusticana|qid=Q11345564}}.
* Around the satomiya, Tsurugaike Park is developed, and hot springs are nearby.

== Other ==
Possibly due to faith around Shirataki Kannon, treated as this shrine's inner sanctuary, it is unusual for a {{ill|Shugendō|ca|Shugendo|cs|Šugendó|de|Shugendō|es|Shugendō|fr|Shugendō|it|Shugendō|ja|修験道|ko|수험도|pl|Shugendō|pt|Shugendō|ru|Сюгэндо|simple|Shugendō|sk|Šugendó|sr|Šugendo|tr|Shugendō|zh|修驗道|qid=Q1483875}} mountain in that women were not prohibited from old times.
